Within Temptation is a Dutch symphonic metal band founded in 1996 by vocalist Sharon den Adel and guitarist Robert Westerholt. Known for their fusion of powerful metal riffs and orchestral elements, they have become a cornerstone of the symphonic metal genre. Their debut album, *Enter* (1997), showcased a gothic metal style, but it was their second album, *Mother Earth* (2000), that catapulted them to fame with the hit single "Ice Queen," which topped the charts in the Netherlands and Belgium.

The band solidified their international presence with *The Silent Force* (2004), featuring a full orchestra and choir, and *The Heart of Everything* (2007), which introduced them to a wider global audience. Their fifth album, *The Unforgiving* (2011), brought a fresh sound blending rock and pop influences, complemented by a comic book series and short films. *Hydra* (2014) expanded their versatility with collaborations featuring artists like Howard Jones and Tarja Turunen. 

In 2019, *Resist* modernized their symphonic sound with contemporary influences, while their most recent album, *Bleed Out* (2023), continues their musical evolution. Major hits include "Ice Queen," "Stand My Ground," "Angels," "Faster," and "Paradise (What About Us?)." 

With numerous awards and a global fanbase, Within Temptation remains one of the most celebrated acts in symphonic metal, renowned for their dynamic live performances and genre-defining sound.
album_description:
The Silent Force is the third studio album by Dutch symphonic metal band Within Temptation, released on 15 November 2004, by GUN Records. On 5 August 2008, The Silent Force along with Mother Earth were released in the United States by Roadrunner Records. This album is the first to feature Ruud Jolie on lead guitar, as well as Martijn Spierenburg on keyboards, after Martijn Westerholt had to leave the band due to illness. It is also the first to feature Daniel Gibson as their producer. The album deepened the band symphonic approach, this time featuring more atmospheric songs that resemble the predominant fantasistic lyrics, inspired both by literature and the band members personal lives.
The album spawned three singles that helped increasing the band's popularity in Europe, all of them achieving commercial success in their homeland and several other European countries. The first single, "Stand My Ground", was released in November 2004 and reached the fourth position on the Dutch Top 40. The second single, "Memories", was released on 31 January 2005. The third and final single, "Angels", was released on 13 June 2005.

Kamelot is an American power metal band from Tampa, Florida, formed by Thomas Youngblood in 1987. The Black Halo is the seventh studio album by American power metal band Kamelot. It was released on March 15, 2005, through Steamhammer Records. It is a concept album inspired by Goethe's Faust. Continuing the story introduced in Epica, it is the second and final record in Kamelot's two-part rock opera about Ariel. Epica tells Part 1 while The Black Halo tells Part 2. Goethe's Faust is also broken into two parts. The Black Halo features guest appearances by Simone Simons, Shagrath, Jens Johansson, and several others. The album was released on vinyl in the spring of 2009, along with Ghost Opera.

Manifest is the sixth studio album by Swedish heavy metal band Amaranthe. It was released on 2 October 2020 via Nuclear Blast.
The album features guest appearances from Noora Louhimo of Battle Beast, Perttu Kivilaakso of Apocalyptica, Elias Holmlid of Dragonland, and Heidi Shepherd of Butcher Babies.
In an interview with HeadBangers Lifestyle, the band's guitarist and keyboardist Olof Mörck revealed that the album version of "Do or Die" will only contain Nils Molin's male clean vocals and Henrik Englund Wilhemsson's unclean vocals, while the single version of the song, which will appear as a bonus track on the album, only contains Elize Ryd's female clean vocals and Angela Gossow's harsh vocals. The guitar solo by Jeff Loomis appears on both versions of the song. It is also the final album to feature Wilhemsson before his departure from the band on June 8, 2022.
